message.content:
Let \(N=\overline{abcd}\). Since \(\overline{ab}\) divides \(N\),

\[
N=100\overline{ab}+\overline{cd},
\]

so \(\overline{ab}\mid \overline{cd}\).

To minimize \(N\), try the smallest leading digits.

- If \(a>1\), then \(N\ge 2111\).
- If \(a=1\) and \(b\ge2\), then \(N\ge1211\).

So any candidate smaller than \(1155\) must start with \(11\). Then \(\overline{ab}=11\), so \(\overline{cd}\) must be a multiple of \(11\). For \(N<1155\), the only possibilities are:

\[
1111,\ 1122,\ 1133,\ 1144.
\]

Check \(\overline{bc}\) divides each:

- \(1111\): \(\overline{ab}=\overline{bc}=\overline{cd}=11\), not distinct.
- \(1122\): \(\overline{bc}=12\), but \(1122\not\equiv0\pmod{12}\).
- \(1133\): \(\overline{bc}=13\), but \(1133\not\equiv0\pmod{13}\).
- \(1144\): \(\overline{bc}=14\), but \(1144\not\equiv0\pmod{14}\).

Now test \(1155\):

\[
\overline{ab}=11,\quad \overline{bc}=15,\quad \overline{cd}=55.
\]

They are distinct, and

\[
1155\div 11=105,\qquad 1155\div 15=77,\qquad 1155\div 55=21.
\]

Thus \(1155\) works and no smaller number does.

The answer is 1155.
